abstract:
To evaluate damage in patients with hereditary recurrent fever syndromes (HRFs) and other autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) in the Eurofever registry.
Damage was assessed at enrolment in Eurofever using the Autoinflammatory Disease Damage Index (ADDI); multivariable logistic regression was used to identify features associated with damage compared to PFAPA. Longitudinal changes in the ADDI were evaluated in patients with follow-up data.
Overall, 3575 patients were enrolled from 30 countries with a median age at enrolment of 12 years. Among HRFs, CAPS had the highest prevalence of damage (59/131, 45%), whereas FMF the lowest (167/1483, 11.3%); the most relevant damage domains were sensorineural hearing loss in CAPS (36/131, 27.5%) and renal damage/amyloidosis in MKD (11/100, 11%). Among other AIDs, damage was most common in undefined AIDs (111/257, 43.2%) and DADA2 (41/96, 42.7%); musculoskeletal damage predominated in CNO/CRMO (162/494, 32.8%) and neurological damage in DADA2 (22/96, 22.9%). The ADDI was limited in capturing damage in the gastrointestinal, vascular, and peripheral nervous systems. Diagnosis (highest OR: undefined AIDs, OR 13.4, 95% CI: 7.5-23.9), older age at enrolment, and ongoing specific therapy were independently associated with damage (AUC 0.76). ADDI items generally decreased over time, without establishing reversal of irreversible damage.
Damage was highly variable in the cohort depending on the disease. The ADDI was useful for damage assessment in HRFs and other AIDs; further improvements of the tool should include additional damage domains, refinement of some items, clearer distinction from disease activity, and a better evaluation of longitudinal damage.

title: Damage burden in autoinflammatory diseases: Insights from the autoinflammatory disease damage index in the international Eurofever registry.
